instantiated_cells.justification: Lobbying as a lobbyist generally requires licensure and authorization (§13.66), and an individual paid by a principal whose duties include lobbying is a 'lobbyist' (§13.62(11)), though a principal/lobbyist may avoid licensing/registration/reporting if a verified statement is filed and expenditures stay ≤$500/year (§13.621(5)).
A lobbyist must obtain a license (file an application) and the license expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, so filing is required biennially rather than at least once per year.

The law requires lobbyists to file a license application (§13.63) and separately requires principals exceeding the threshold to file a registration statement (§13.64), indicating separate filings by each party.
Elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees are not subject to specified lobbying requirements when acting in an official capacity.

An agency that files a statement under §13.695 and officials named in it are not subject to several key lobbying provisions (e.g., licensing/registration/reporting restrictions), except as provided in §13.695.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text sets change-notification deadlines for principals (e.g., agency statements under §13.695(2)) but provides no general deadline for lobbyists to notify the commission of changes to their lobbyist license/registration information.

The statute requires a lobbyist to be licensed and authorized before lobbying (§13.66) but does not specify a numeric 'days after first lobbying' deadline; the only numeric day triggers in the bundle are principal-side (e.g., principal registration within 10 days after exceeding $500 in §13.64(1)).
No provision in the bundled sections addresses submitting a photograph with a lobbyist license application or principal registration; if required, it would have to appear in forms/rules not included.
